not_modelled.what: Exemption of up to 10,000 for a return (reduced by the AGI test, gone at 80,000 joint or 65,000 others) of Civil Service Retirement System income or income from a contributory system of the U.S. government or a state government, another state's included. It is taken in place of the Social Security exemption and needs benefits based on earnings not covered by Social Security. A projection does not hold that fact, and a New York State or other public pension whose earnings paid Social Security tax does not qualify.

Percentage capital gains exclusion: 40% of eligible gain on assets held more than three years, up to 350,000, in place of the 5,000 flat exclusion when larger. Homes, depreciable personal property and publicly traded securities are not eligible, and a projection does not know the kind of asset sold.
Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled: 24% of the federal Schedule R credit. A projection does not compute the federal credit, and it can apply to a disabled person of any age.
Additional 1,250 of standard deduction for each person who is blind.
Interest on U.S. obligations (Treasury bonds, bills and notes) is subtracted (Schedule IN-112 Line 7); a projection does not split it from other interest.

Interest on bonds of the Vermont Student Assistance Corporation, Build America, the Vermont Telecommunications Authority and the Vermont Public Power Supply Authority is subtracted (Schedule IN-112 Line 15).

Vermont adds 24% of the federal additional tax on qualified plans including IRA, HSA and MSA, so an early IRA withdrawal pays this as well as the federal additional tax (Schedule IN-119 Lines 1, 4 and 5).

Medical Expenses Deduction (Schedule IN-112 Line 11): federal Schedule A medical expenses, less non-allowable ones, above the Vermont standard deduction and exemptions. It matters for a household with high medical or care costs.

Lines held in the record notes: 24% of tax on lump-sum distributions and of investment credit recapture, student loan interest, the Child Care Contribution on self-employment income, the charitable, other-state, child care, child, earned income and veteran credits, and the Property Tax and Renter Credits.

approximations.what: The 10,000 retirement exemption for CSRS and other systems is not applied, for any pension. Modelling it on the kind of pension alone would give it to members whose earnings paid Social Security tax, who do not qualify.
approximations.size: Only for a return with such a pension: at most 10,000 of income, about 660 of tax at the 6.6% rate, and less when the Social Security exemption is the better election.

approximations.what: The 5,000 flat gains exclusion is applied to all gains. Schedule IN-153 takes only long-term gains, less Schedule D Lines 18 and 19 and investment interest, and limits the exclusion to 40% of federal taxable income.
approximations.size: At most 5,000 of income, about 438 of tax at the 8.75% rate; the income limit bites only under 12,500 of federal taxable income.

approximations.what: All municipal bond interest is treated as from other states and taxed; interest on Vermont obligations is not added on Schedule IN-112.
approximations.size: Vermont bond interest at the household's rate, 3.35% to 8.75%.

approximations.what: The rate schedule is one continuous schedule: the printed rows that restart at 75,000 are merged and printed base taxes, rounded to the dollar, are not used. Below 75,000 the booklet uses tax tables in 100 dollar rows.
approximations.size: About a dollar a year at most outside the first table row.

approximations.what: Minimum tax (recapture, effect other): above 150,000 of federal AGI the tax is the greater of the schedule tax and 3% of federal AGI less interest from U.S. obligations. The projection uses federal AGI and does not take off the interest. It bites only when subtractions and exemptions are large, such as Railroad Retirement, a percentage gains exclusion or several dependents.
approximations.size: 3% of the U.S. obligations interest when the minimum applies: 300 on 10,000 of interest.
